pattern: Cannot assign to a const binding
hint: Use a mutable declaration without const if this binding must change. Loop variables and protected fields cannot be assigned directly.
Initialize the const binding where it is declared, for example: const count: int = 1;
Add a final fallback arm: default -> value;
Remove or combine the repeated case; each value can appear only once.
Use a literal such as 1 or "open", or an enum value, as the case label.
Make the result match its declared type. Use an explicit conversion only when that conversion is supported.
Iterate an array, List, Set, Map, or string. Check nullable collections against null first.
Copy the value to a local binding if needed, then guard its use with if(value != null).
Assign a value on every path before reading it; a loop may execute zero times.
Check the spelling, declare the name in this scope, or import the class that defines it.
Check the receiver's type and member spelling. Use me.member for the current object's members.
End this declaration or expression with a semicolon.
Match the argument count and order in the method or constructor declaration.
